title: Synechococcus Culture and Transformation
author: Yibo Wu
materials: BG-11 agar plates Add 15 g of agar to 200 mL of Gibco™ BG-11 medium in an autoclavable flask. Note: Use high quality agar, such as Calbiochem, Cat. No.12177, or Sigma, Cat. No. A1296. Autoclave on liquid cycle for 20 minutes. Warm 800 mL of Gibco™ BG-11 medium to 55–60°C in a water bath. After autoclaving, cool the agar containing flask to ~55°C. Combine the agar containing flask with 800 mL of Gibco™ BG-11 medium. Add spectinomycin to a final concentration of 10 µg/mL (if required), and pour into 10-cm plates. Let the plates harden (do not over dry), invert them, and store at 2–8°C in the dark. Final agar concentration will be 1.5%.

Do not thaw more than 3 vials at a time. Frozen S. elongatus cells are very sensitive to temperature fluctuations. Before the cells are thawed, the cells must be transferred from the −80°C freezer into a dry ice container as quickly as possible and the vials should be buried in dry ice. To maximize the recovery of the cells when thawing, warm the cells very quickly by placing the tubes directly from the dry ice container into a 34°C water bath. When the cells are completely thawed, immediately dilute them into Gibco™ BG-11 medium, pre-warmed to room temperature. You can count the S. elongatus cells using the Attune™ NxT Acoustic Focusing Cytometer (or equivalent) by detecting the endogenous orange-fluorescent phycoerythrin and red-fluorescent chlorophyll. For more information, contact Cell Analysis Technical Support Center (www.thermofisher.com/support).

Grow the cells using Gibco™ BG-11 medium (Cat. nos. A1379901, A1379902), which is specifically formulated for optimal growth and maintenance of S. elongatus cells. Grow S. elongatus liquid cultures at 34°C ± 1°C with CO₂ (1–2% in air) under continuous illumination using moderate light intensities of cool fluorescent white (50–100 µE m⁻² s⁻¹) with agitation on a gyratory shaker set to 100 rpm. Note: S. elongatus cultures can also be grown using light intensities of 50–400 µE m⁻² s⁻¹ with only atmospheric CO₂ (i.e., without additional CO₂). The presence of CO₂ is needed to obtain optimal growth of S. elongatus in liquid culture as it is a photosynthetic organism; however, additional CO₂ is not necessary during transformation where the cells are grown on agar support and are exposed to atmospheric CO₂. If you are bubbling the culture with CO₂ enriched air or CO₂ gas, prepare the BG-11 medium with 50 mM NaHCO₃ and adjust the pH to 7.5. The presence of NaHCO₃ in the medium prevents it from becoming acidic.

steps.title: Prepare LB Medium
steps.instruction: Prepare 1 liter of LB medium and autoclave.

substeps.instruction: Dissolve 10 g tryptone, 5 g yeast extract, and 10 g NaCl in 950 mL of deionized water.
Adjust pH to 7.0 using NaOH and bring the final volume to 1 liter.
Autoclave on a liquid cycle for 20 minutes at 15 psi.
Cool the solution to 55°C and add appropriate antibiotics if needed (e.g., spectinomycin at a final concentration of 100 µg/mL).
Store the medium at room temperature or at 2–8°C.

steps.title: Prepare LB Agar Plates
steps.instruction: Prepare LB agar plates using the LB medium recipe.

substeps.instruction: Prepare LB medium as described above, adding 15 g/L agar before autoclaving.
Autoclave on a liquid cycle for 20 minutes at 15 psi.
Cool the medium to ~55°C and add appropriate antibiotics.
Pour into 10-cm plates, allow the agar to harden, then invert and store at 2–8°C in the dark.

steps.title: Thaw Synechococcus Cells
steps.instruction: Carefully thaw frozen S. elongatus PCC 7942 cells to maintain viability.

substeps.instruction: Remove frozen cells from −80°C storage and immediately bury the vial(s) in dry ice to minimize temperature fluctuations.
Place the vial in a 34°C water bath and thaw quickly until the last ice crystal melts (~2 minutes), ensuring the vial is not agitated or swirled.
Wipe the outside of the vial with 70% ethanol and place in a rack at room temperature.

steps.title: Resuscitate and Grow Cultures
steps.instruction: Inoculate and grow cells in an algal growth chamber until they reach the required density.

substeps.instruction: Add 6 mL of room-temperature pre-warmed Gibco™ BG-11 medium into each well of a 6-well plate.
Transfer 100 µL of thawed cells into each well.
Place plates in an algal growth chamber at 34°C ± 1°C with 1% CO₂ and constant light of 50 µE m⁻² s⁻¹ (do not exceed 50 µE m⁻² s⁻¹ immediately after resuscitation; do not stack plates).
Incubate with gentle agitation on a gyratory shaker at 100 rpm.
On Day 2, measure OD₇₅₀ by transferring 400 µL of cell suspension into a disposable plastic cuvette containing 400 µL of Gibco™ BG-11 medium.
Continue incubation until OD₇₅₀ is ≥ 1.

steps.title: Prepare Cells for Transformation
steps.instruction: Harvest and concentrate cells to the appropriate density for transformation.

substeps.instruction: Measure the OD₇₅₀ of the culture (optimal range is between 1 and 2).
Harvest 1.5 mL of cells per transformation by centrifugation at 14,000 rpm for 3 minutes at room temperature.
Remove the supernatant by pipetting.
Resuspend cells in 1 mL of Gibco™ BG-11 medium by gently pipetting up and down.
Centrifuge again at 14,000 rpm for 1 minute at room temperature and remove the supernatant.
Resuspend the final cell pellet in 100 µL of Gibco™ BG-11 medium by gently pipetting up and down.

steps.title: Perform Transformation
steps.instruction: Introduce plasmid DNA into the cells and incubate.

substeps.instruction: Add 100 ng of supercoiled plasmid DNA (e.g., pSyn_6 construct) to the resuspended cells.
Prepare a negative control by adding 100 ng of empty pSyn_6 vector to a separate tube of cells.
Mix the DNA-cell suspension gently by flicking the tube.
Incubate the mixtures in a 34°C water bath with a dark lid for 4 hours.
Remove tubes from the water bath and wipe with 70% ethanol.

steps.title: Plate and Incubate Transformants
steps.instruction: Plate the transformation mixture on selective media and grow colonies.

substeps.instruction: Pre-warm selective BG-11 + spectinomycin plates (10 µg/mL spectinomycin) to room temperature for 1 hour before plating.
Plate 80 µL and 5 µL of each transformation mixture on separate pre-warmed plates.
Place plates agar-side down on illuminated shelves at room temperature (25–30°C), ensuring plates are not stacked.
Incubate for 5–7 days or until colonies are ready to pick.
